title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-16
content:
Notes to self - continuous batching throughput regression (late Feb 2026)

Summary
- Observed throughput drop on a subset of hosted nodes after config change rolled on 2026-02-18.
- Symptoms: tokens/sec down ~30-45% for small-req workloads (avg seq_len 16). Latency p95 up from 160ms -> 420ms.
- Regression seems tied to continuous-batching config and a changeet that touched batch_timeout_ms + kernel-selection fallback.

Context / recent changes
- 2026-02-17: Rollout of batching policy change (rollout id: rollout/cont-batch-2026-02-17)
  - Changed default batch_timeout_ms: 8 -> 80 (intended to reduce small-batch flapping)
  - Added fallback kernel selector rule: prefer low-mem kernel when sequence_length > 2048 (should be irrelevant for our small seqs)
  - Added header gating code: if header x-redwood-batch=disabled skip batching path

What I see in the field
- Affected hosts: pool-gpu-a-us-west-2, subset of dedicated instances (about 18% of capacity).
- Metric snapshots (hosts before vs after):
  - tokens/sec baseline: 1.2M -> after: 0.72M
  - avg batch size (requests per batch): 6.1 -> 3.2
  - KV cache hit ratio: 82% -> 79% (small drop but not enough to explain throughput loss)
  - CPU poke on host: increased kernel_reloads and more frequent context switches in runtime thread traces

Quick hypotheses
1) batch_timeout_ms increased to 80ms -> causes batching to wait longer for more requests, but paradoxically we see smaller avg batch size. Could be because an internal timer reset bug cancels pending batches when a new request arrives during timeout window.
2) Header gating bug: certain SDK clients accidentally set x-redwood-batch=disabled (or blank) after SDK bump -> these requests bypass continuous batching path and go into per-request slow path.
3) Kernel selector fallback bug inadvertently toggles to slower kernel for small seqs on subset of GPUs due to mis-evaluated condition (off-by-one in architecture id mapping).
4) Autoscaler / pool change caused heterogeneous instances with different runtime versions (mix of 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-18 builds) where new build has a regression.

Repro steps attempted locally
- Ran synthetic load using loadgen from perf repo (scripts/loadgen.py).
Commands used: (run from perf repo)
- python loadgen.py --target-host host-1:8080 --qps 1000 --seq-len 16 --duration 300 --parallel 8 --model redwood-llama-3b
- python loadgen.py --target-host host-1:8080 --qps 1000 --seq-len 512 --duration 300 --parallel 8 --model redwood-llama-3b

Observations:
- Against host with v2026-01-30: throughput stable (tokens/sec ~1.18M), avg batch size ~6.
- Against host with v2026-02-18: tokens/sec ~0.7M, avg batch size ~3, p95 latency spikes.

Logs / snippets (redacted)
- Runtime WARN lines repeated: "batch_manager: timer_cancel failed for batch_id=0x2f4d (already flushed)"
- Error trace on one host: "kernel_selector: unsupported arch id 0x7f, falling back to generic (slower) kernel)"
- SDK header seen in request: "x-redwood-batch": "" (empty) from ip 10.23.5.82, client sdk-version=1.12.0

Commands tried to gather more data
- SSH into bad host and check runtime version + env
- ssh build@pool-gpu-a-us-west-2-07
- ps aux | grep redwood-runtime
- cat /etc/redwood/version (shows v2026-02-18)
- curl -sS localhost:8080/metrics | grep batch_timeout_ms
  -> batch_timeout_ms 80
- curl -sS localhost:8080/metrics | grep avg_batch_size
  -> avg_batch_size 3.1

Test: force batch_timeout_ms back to 8 locally (hotpatch)
- curl -X POST localhost:8080/admin/config -d '{"batch_timeout_ms":8}'
- Observed: avg_batch_size increases slowly back to ~5.8 over a minute, tokens/sec recovers to ~1.1M.
- However this hotpatch is not long-term fix: some hosts still return to low batch size after ~30m.

SDK header hypothesis check
- Grepped ingress logs for x-redwood-batch header values
  - grep -R "x-redwood-batch" /var/log/ingress/http-*.log | grep -v "x-redwood-batch: enabled" | head
  - Found ~4.2% of requests had blank header or explicit "disabled" after SDK 1.12.0 rollout.
- Rollback of SDK rollout to 1.11.3 correlates with partial recovery on affected customer traces.

Kernel selector check
- On affected host: /var/log/runtime/kernel_selector.log shows repeated fallback decisions for arch id mapping 0x7e/0x7f where newer runtime expects mapping table that was updated in a different package.
- Binary diff between v2026-01-30 and v2026-02-18 shows change in arch mapping table initialiser order (off-by-one).

Interim conclusions
- Multiple contributing factors: SDK header regression causing some requests to bypass batching AND runtime change in batch_timeout_ms exposing a timer-related race that cancels batches unexpectedly on some hosts (likely exacerbated by kernel selector fallbacks causing slower kernel times which changes timing windows).
- The SDK header thing accounts for ~4-5% of requests; that doesn't explain 30-45% throughput drop alone. Timer bug + kernel fallback likely account for bulk of regression.

Immediate mitigations applied
- Reverted batch_timeout_ms to 8 on all affected hosts (hotpatch via admin API) -> partial throughput recovery.
- Rollback the runtime deploy to v2026-01-30 for the affected host pool (coordinated rollback started 2026-02-25) -> metrics returned to baseline in rolled-back hosts.
- SDK: flagged SDK release 1.12.0 as problematic, created quick patch to ensure header defaults to "enabled" if missing. Patch PR GH-PR-1247.

Longer-term fix + next steps
- Root cause PRs:
  - runtime: fix timer cancellation race in batch_manager (probable fix branch: fix/batch-timer-race-2026) -> add unit tests to simulate concurrent request arrival during timeout window.
  - runtime: correct arch mapping table initialiser order to prevent accidental fallback for our supported GPUs (PR: GH-PR-1253).
  - sdk: ensure default x-redwood-batch header enforced and add integration tests for header propagation (PR: GH-PR-1247).
- Add e2e perf test in CI that runs with small seq_len workloads and asserts avg_batch_size >= 5 under qps=1000 for model redwood-llama-3b.
- Add canary telemetry that emits per-request flags: "batch_path_taken" boolean and kernel_selector_reason string to make debugging faster.
- Notify SRE and product about customer-affecting impact and coordinate post-mortem (ticket JIRA-INC-4821).

Open questions / unknowns
- Why do some hosts revert to low batch size after hotpatch? (possible mem leak or resource contention causing internal scheduler to evict timers?) Need heap/profiler dump.
- Is there any edge case where batch_timeout_ms=80 could be valid for bursty workloads? Document pros/cons and add safe upper bound check in config schema.

To do (short list)
- [ ] land fix/batch-timer-race-2026 + add unit tests
- [ ] land arch mapping PR and roll out to canary (2 hosts)
- [ ] ship SDK header default patch to new SDK release and gate rollout behind metrics
- [ ] add e2e perf test to CI

Notes: keep this doc informal - will expand after root cause PRs land and we have PM/ops post-mortem info.

Last quick logs appended (paste from bad host 2026-02-22)
- 2026-02-22T18:12:03Z runtime INFO batch_manager: started batch_id=0x2f4d timeout=80ms
- 2026-02-22T18:12:03Z runtime WARN batch_manager: timer_cancel failed for batch_id=0x2f4d (already flushed)
- 2026-02-22T18:12:03Z runtime DEBUG request-handler: header x-redwood-batch="" client=10.23.5.82 sdk=1.12.0
- 2026-02-22T18:12:03Z kernel_selector WARN unsupported arch id 0x7f -> fallback generic kernel

-- avery
